paragraphs.text: Per-workspace MCP and skill switches for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) - one popup per workspace row
# dsh-mcp-manager
English | 中文 · [](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@gyp8735abc/dsh-mcp-manager) · [](LICENSE)
A **per-workspace** MCP and skill manager for DeepSeek Harness.

One button on each workspace row opens a popup where you decide which MCP servers and which
skills t

hat workspace gets. Global MCP, project MCP and skills all switch **independently per
workspace**.
## The problem it solves

DSH's own MCP configuration is **profile-wide**: whatever is in `mcp:` applies to every
workspace an
d every session. In daily use that means:

- `codebase` is useful in project A and in project B, but the two projects keep different
`.codebase

/codebase.db` files — one global config can only point at one of them.
- You keep five MCP servers a

round, but this workspace needs one. The other four hold their
processes open and stuff the tool lis

t, so the model picks the wrong tool more often.
- The same for skills: the dozens under `~/.claude/

skills` show up in every session although
only a couple of workspaces really want them.
This plugin moves the switches down to the **workspace** layer:
| Object | Source | Switch granularity |

| Global MCP | `mcpServers` in `~/.claude.json` | per workspace |
| Project MCP | the workspace's ow

n `.mcp.json` | per workspace |
| Manual MCP | hand-written `dsh-mcp-client` rows in the profile | p

er workspace |
| Skills | `.dsh/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.agents/skills`, `~/.dsh/skills`, `~/.cl
aude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills` | per workspace |
## Features

- **One popup for everything** — grouped into project MCP / global MCP / manual MCP / project
skills

/ global skills, one switch per row, with `Enabled`/`Disabled` and
`Connected`/`Not connected` show

n inline.
- **Real per-workspace isolation** — the state key is the workspace path; a server you tur

n
off in A stays on in B.
- **Union mounting** — every workspace with a live session keeps its own M

CP servers mounted,
one process per (workspace, server) with its own config and `cwd`. Focusing or s

witching a
session never stops another workspace's servers; a workspace's servers unload with its la

st
session.
- **Session-scoped tool filtering** — only this workspace's `mcp__<workspace>__*` tools

plus
global/manual ones reach the current session, so another live workspace's tools never leak in.

- **Skills filtered the same way** — a disabled skill disappears from the model's catalog and
from `

/name` injection, and a direct `skill` tool call is refused with an explicit reason.
- **Claude Code

skill compatibility** — project `.claude/skills` and user `~/.claude/skills`
are scanned, including

`SKILL.md` files without YAML frontmatter.
- **Dynamic rescan** — every popup open re-reads the wor

kspace list and each workspace's
`.mcp.json`, so new workspaces and edited configs apply without res

tarting DSH.
- **Zero core patches** — nothing inside the DSH installation is modified; installing o

r
removing the plugin only touches the profile and `$DSH_HOME`.
- **Bilingual UI** — follows the DSH
interface language (English / 简体中文).
## Install
### Option 1: plugin market (three steps)

1. Turn the tab on first: **Plugins → Experimental plugins → enable “Custom plugin markets”**.
(It i

s an optional experimental bundle; the **Discover** tab only exists once it is installed.
You do thi

s once.)
2. **Discover → Add index source**, and enter:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
3. Search for `MCP manager`, `mcp`, `workspace` or `gyp8735abc`, open the entry, press **Install**.

> Market indexes are unsigned; titles, authors and sources are publisher claims. Only add
> index so

urces you trust, and check in the confirmation dialog that the source is
> `@gyp8735abc/dsh-mcp-mana

ger`.
>
> A "plugin market" is not an app store: DSH has no central store, the market only reads the

> index URLs **you** add. Besides the index above you can add the community index this plugin
> is

submitted to — `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/dsh-plugin-catalog/index.json`
> (the Awesome DSH Plugi
n catalog) — and search there.
### Option 2: one command
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The package is also a DSH bundle (`dsh.bundle.patch`), so the plugin row is inserted into the
profil
e composition automatically — no hand-written `cordis.patch.yml` needed.
## Compatibility
| Item | Requirement |

| DSH | `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0` (checked against the running version at install time) |
| Node.js | `>

=22` |
| Surface | Web only (`dsh web` and the desktop GUI's web view); `headless` / `acp` have no U
Surface | Web only (`dsh web` and the desktop GUI's web view); `headless` / `acp` have no UI entry |

The only runtime dependencies are packages that ship with the DSH installation
(`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mc
p-client` etc.); the plugin itself has none.
## Known limitations

- **No skill file watcher** — a skill added to `.claude/skills` while DSH is running appears after
a

restart (existing and project skills all load at startup).
- **The workspace button is DOM-injected

** — DSH 0.2.x declares slots for session rows only, so
the button is inserted with a `MutationObser

ver` and re-added after re-renders. If it does not
show up, first check that the DSH version is insi

de `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`.
- **The skill filter patches a prototype** — it affects every consumer of

the skill service (for
example a skill picker UI). That is intended: the switch is per workspace and

every lookup
carries the `cwd`.
- **State is not in the DSH settings page** — DSH 0.2.x no longer l

ets a plugin claim an arbitrary
settings namespace, so the switches live in the plugin's own `state.

json`.
- **Non-active workspaces only save state** — they do not spawn processes eagerly, which keep

s
unused workspaces from holding servers open.
## Security

- The plugin spawns the **stdio commands** declared in project `.mcp.json` files and
`~/.claude.json

` — that is the same trust you would give that configuration. Only use it with
repositories and conf

igs you trust.
- The three HTTP endpoints are **unauthenticated**; the design assumes `dsh web` list

ens on
loopback only (the default `127.0.0.1`). With `--host 0.0.0.0`, anyone who can reach the port

can toggle your MCP servers.
- The plugin never modifies the DSH installation and never writes `set

tings.yaml`; its only write
is `$DSH_HOME/mcp-manager/state.json`.
